text: The grocery delivery arrived with two cartons of oat milk packed directly on top of fresh peaches and ripe avocados, squashing them into pulp.
author: Serena Vitale

text: Ordered lactose-free whole milk and organic eggs, but the picker substituted regular cow milk without sending any SMS or in-app approval notification.
author: Alberto Gatti

text: Fresh tagliatelle pasta was delivered with an expiration date of tomorrow! You cannot send near-expired refrigerated food on grocery delivery orders.
author: Claudio Fontana

text: Raw salmon and minced beef arrived at room temperature. The delivery bag contained no insulated thermal sleeve or ice gel packs on a 28-degree afternoon.
author: Daniela Lombardi

text: Half of the organic eggs in the dozen carton were cracked because the bag was dropped or roughly handled by the dispatch team.
author: Fabio Serra

text: Picker substituted gluten-free flour with standard wheat flour without asking. This is dangerous for customers with celiac disease.
author: Silvia Mancini

text: Fragile produce like berries and tomatoes should never be packed at the bottom of grocery bags under heavy laundry detergent bottles.
author: Enrico Barbieri

text: Ordered 5 key dinner ingredients and 2 were missing from the sealed paper grocery sack, yet I was billed for the full total.
author: Cristina Rossi

text: Delivery arrived within 30 minutes, but poor bag packing standards resulted in crushed bakery bread and bruised bananas.
author: Paolo Marini
